message.abstract:
<jats:title>Forming the Moon from Earth</jats:title>
          <jats:p>
            It is thought that the Moon formed after a Mars-sized planet hit Earth about 4.5 billion years ago. Computer simulations of this event predict that the Moon was produced primarily from material from the impacting planet. However, the Moon has a similar composition to that of Earth, and the impacting planet would likely have had a different composition. Prior models assumed that the impact left the Earth-Moon system with the same angular momentum as it has today (see the Perspective by
            <jats:bold>
              <jats:related-article xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" ext-link-type="doi" issue="6110" page="1040" related-article-type="in-this-issue" vol="338" xlink:href="10.1126/science.1229954">Halliday</jats:related-article>
            </jats:bold>
            ).
            <jats:bold>Ćuk and Stewart</jats:bold>
            (p.
            <jats:related-article xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" ext-link-type="doi" page="1047" related-article-type="in-this-issue" vol="338" xlink:href="10.1126/science.1225542">1047</jats:related-article>
            , published online 17 October; see the cover) show that the angular momentum of the Earth-Moon system could have decreased by half after the Moon-forming impact, opening the door to new impact models. For example, simulations suggest that high-velocity impacts onto a fast-spinning early Earth can lead to a Moon formed primarily from Earth's mantle.
            <jats:bold>Canup</jats:bold>
            (p.
            <jats:related-article xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" ext-link-type="doi" page="1052" related-article-type="in-this-issue" vol="338" xlink:href="10.1126/science.1226073">1052</jats:related-article>
            , published online 17 October) considered instead lower-velocity impacts by planets comparable in mass to the proto-Earth, which could generate a Moon and an Earth with similar compositions.
          </jats:p>
title: Forming a Moon with an Earth-like Composition via a Giant Impact
